transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I guess things have just been really extreme for me at work lately. I went from launching nonstop plant redesign projects, calling our suppliers way after hours, and basically rewriting the entire shift plan by myself... to suddenly being completely unable to keep up with the very plans I had just set in motion. I just hit a wall, and I don't really know what's going on with me.
During that period when you were working nonstop on the plant redesign, did you find you needed much less sleep than usual—like only a few hours—without feeling tired the next day?

Yeah, that's exactly what happened. I was getting maybe two or three hours of sleep a night. But I didn't feel tired at all. I'd show up at the plant the next morning feeling completely sharp and charged. It honestly felt like sleep was just optional... like it was kind of an inefficient use of my time when I had all those projects going.
Before this recent period of high energy, have you ever had a distinct episode—lasting two weeks or more—where you felt persistently sad, low, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Actually, that's kind of what I'm dealing with right now since I hit that wall. Lately, I just... I wake up in the temporary apartment with this really heavy, hollow feeling. It honestly feels like the day is already ruined before I even drive to the plant. And, yeah, I've definitely had stretches like this in the past, too, before all the redesign projects started, where that exact feeling just hangs over me for weeks.

latest_inference.note: Confirmed history of both a manic episode (decreased need for sleep, elevated energy, grandiosity/hyperproductivity) and prior distinct depressive episodes, consistent with Bipolar I Disorder. This rules out F30.9 (Manic Episode alone) since depressive episodes are also present, and rules out unipolar depression given the clear manic episode.
